examples.solution_text:
At the $y$-axis, $x=0$, so $y=5$. Between $y=2$ and $y=5$, the radius is $|x|=5-y$.
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=(5-y)^{2}\\V&=\pi\int_{2}^{5}(5-y)^{2}\,dy\\&=\pi\left[-\frac{(5-y)^{3}}{3}\right]_{2}^{5}\\&=\pi\left(0-(-9)\right)\\&=9\pi\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

At $x=3$, $y=3^{2}-3=6$, so the limits are $y=-3$ and $y=6$.
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=y+3\\V&=\pi\int_{-3}^{6}(y+3)\,dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}+3y\right]_{-3}^{6}\\&=\pi\left(36-\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\frac{81\pi}{2}\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

Write the squared radius in terms of $y$.
$\begin{align*}x&=y^{1/3}\\x^{2}&=y^{2/3}\\V&=\pi\int_{0}^{27}y^{2/3}\,dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{3}{5}y^{5/3}\right]_{0}^{27}\\&=\frac{3\pi}{5}(243)\\&=\frac{729\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

Rearrange for $x$, then square and expand before integrating.
$\begin{align*}y^{2}&=x-2\\x&=y^{2}+2\\x^{2}&=y^{4}+4y^{2}+4\\V&=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(y^{4}+4y^{2}+4\right)\,dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{y^{5}}{5}+\frac{4y^{3}}{3}+4y\right]_{0}^{1}\\&=\pi\left(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{4}{3}+4\right)\\&=\frac{83\pi}{15}\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

Use the inverse relationship between logarithms and exponentials.
$\begin{align*}x&=e^{y}\\x^{2}&=e^{2y}\\V&=\pi\int_{0}^{2}e^{2y}\,dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{e^{2y}}{2}\right]_{0}^{2}\\&=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(e^{4}-1\right)\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

At the $y$-axis, $y(y-4)=0$, giving $y=0$ and $y=4$. Between these limits, $x\leq0$, so the radius is $|x|=y(4-y)$.
$\begin{align*}x^{2}&=y^{2}(4-y)^{2}\\&=y^{4}-8y^{3}+16y^{2}\\V&=\pi\int_{0}^{4}\left(y^{4}-8y^{3}+16y^{2}\right)\,dy\\&=\pi\left[\frac{y^{5}}{5}-2y^{4}+\frac{16y^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{4}\\&=\pi\left(\frac{1024}{5}-512+\frac{1024}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{512\pi}{15}\ \text{units}^{3}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: The axis intersection gives y=5. The radius is 5-y on [2,5], so V=π∫₂⁵(5-y)²dy=9π cubic units. The diagram correctly bounds the left-side triangular region.
At x=3, y=6. Since x²=y+3, V=π[y²/2+3y] from -3 to 6=π(36+9/2)=81π/2 cubic units. The right-hand branch and upper boundary agree with the prompt.
For y=x³, x²=y^(2/3). Thus V=(3π/5)27^(5/3)=729π/5 cubic units. The plotted cubic reaches (3,27), matching the upper boundary.
Rearrangement gives x=y²+2 and x²=y⁴+4y²+4. Integrating from 0 to 1 gives π(1/5+4/3+4)=83π/15 cubic units. The curve endpoints (2,0) and (3,1) match the diagram.
The inverse relationship gives x=e^y, hence V=π∫₀²e^(2y)dy=π(e⁴-1)/2 cubic units. The diagram closes the region at y=2 and plots the logarithmic boundary consistently.
From y=1/x², x²=1/y. Therefore V=π[ln y] from 2 to 8=πln4 cubic units. The positive branch and both horizontal boundaries match the stated region.

Axis intersections occur at y=0 and y=4. The radius is y(4-y), whose square is y⁴-8y³+16y². Integration gives π(1024/5-512+1024/3)=512π/15 cubic units. The diagram correctly places the bounded region left of the axis.
